title: Causal Analysis of the Offense-Defense Gap: Which Specific Sub-Capabilities Drive the Asymmetry?

original_idea.body:
# Causal Analysis of the Offense-Defense Gap: Which Specific Sub-Capabilities Drive the Asymmetry?

**Problem:** Potter et al. find AI benefits attackers over defenders, but do not decompose which specific sub-capabilities (code generation, natural language synthesis, planning, memory) drive the asymmetry.

**Direction:** Build a matrix of 10 offensive tasks and 10 defensive tasks. For each, identify the primary AI sub-capabilities required (code generation, text synthesis, planning, retrieval). Measure current model performance on each task/capability combination using available benchmarks. Map which sub-capabilities are more offense-biased.

**Why it matters:** If the offense-defense gap is driven by 1-2 specific sub-capabilities, targeted governance interventions (e.g., restricting automated planning in certain contexts) may be more efficient than broad restrictions.

**Relevant context:** Potter et al. arXiv:2504.05408; Kraprayoon HACCA paper; Linder et al. Technical Complexity dimension.
